mainTopic: The source for adding ordinary time onto holy time (תוספת): רבי עקיבא learns it from שביעית, רבי ישמעאל from יום הכפורים
overview: This amud first finishes a discussion about the יובל year. The רבנן say the fiftieth year counts only as יובל, not also as the first year of the next שמיטה cycle, which rejects רבי יהודה. The גמרא then asks for the source of the rule that we add ordinary time onto holy time (מוסיפין מחול על קודש). A ברייתא brings רבי עקיבא, who learns it from 'בחריש ובקציר תשבות': no plowing in year six for שביעית and no harvesting שביעית crops in year eight. רבי ישמעאל reads that verse differently and uses it to permit harvesting the עומר, so the גמרא asks where he learns the rule. He learns it from the יום הכפורים verse 'ועניתם את נפשותיכם בתשעה... בערב': we start fasting while it is still day, add time at the end too, and apply this to שבת and ימים טובים. Finally the גמרא asks what רבי עקיבא learns from that verse. He uses it for the teaching of חייא בר רב מדפתי that eating on the ninth is credited by the verse. That sentence finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: How the רבנן use the verse: the fiftieth year is not double-counted
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use the verse to teach that the fiftieth year (יובל) is counted only as יובל. It is not also the first year of the next שמיטה cycle. This rejects רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, how do they use this verse? It teaches: you count the fiftieth year, but you do not count the fiftieth year as the next cycle's year too. This rejects רבי יהודה, who said the fiftieth year counts both here and there. The verse teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן learn from the verse, since they do not need it for the point the other opinion learned from it. It answers that they use it to reject רבי יהודה's double-counting of the fiftieth year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every extra word in a פסוק must teach something, so each opinion needs a use for this verse. For the רבנן, the verse means: the fiftieth year belongs only to יובל, and the new seven-year שמיטה cycle starts in year fifty-one. רבי יהודה held the fiftieth year is both יובל and year one of the next cycle, and the verse says no.

keyTerms.meaning: Counts for here and for there (counts double)
It teaches us (the new point being made)

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, יובל is its own year. The next שמיטה cycle starts only after it, in year fifty-one. רבי יהודה disagrees and counts year fifty double.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the structure of the שמיטה and יובל calendar: whether each cycle lasts 49 or 50 years.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: Short question: what do the רבנן learn from this verse?

phrases.english: The fiftieth year you count,
phrases.notes: You count it as the יובל year.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מוֹנֶה שְׁנַת חֲמִשִּׁים וְאַחַת —
phrases.english: but you do not count the fiftieth year and one (as the first of the next cycle) —
phrases.notes: Following רש"י: year fifty doesn't also count as year one of the next cycle.

phrases.english: to exclude Rabbi Yehuda, who said:
the fiftieth year counts for here and for there,
phrases.notes: It counts both as יובל and as year one of the next שמיטה cycle.

phrases.english: it teaches us that it does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the earlier discussion (earlier) about the verse on the יובל year by giving the רבנן's use of it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What do the רבנן learn from the verse, if they do not need it for the other opinion's point?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It teaches that the fiftieth year is not counted double, which rejects רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Where do we learn that we add ordinary time onto holy time?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic and asks for the source of the rule of adding ordinary time onto holy time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the rule that we add from the ordinary onto the holy, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The idea of time being 'extended' just came up, so the גמרא now asks for the source of a related rule. This is a setup line that prepares the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the topic was whether יובל stretches into the next year. Now the גמרא asks about a general principle: holy periods get extra time added at their edges. It wants a פסוק as the source.

keyTerms.meaning: We add from the ordinary onto the holy (תוספת: extra time added around a holy period)
From where do we know it? (asking for a source)

steps.whyThisMatters: תוספת is the basis for practices like starting שבת and יום טוב a bit early.

phrases.english: And that we add from the ordinary onto the holy —
from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the יובל discussion to a related general principle about extending holy time.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for adding ordinary time onto holy time.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: no plowing before the seventh year, no harvesting after it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא cites רבי עקיבא. He reads 'בחריש ובקציר תשבות' as banning plowing in year six that helps שביעית, and harvesting שביעית crops in year eight. This shows time is added around שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'In plowing and in harvest you shall rest.' רבי עקיבא says: The verse does not need to tell us about plowing and harvesting in the seventh year itself, because it already said 'Your field you shall not sow.' Rather, it means plowing in the year before שביעית that helps the seventh year, and harvesting the seventh year's crops after the seventh year has ended.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. רבי עקיבא says the verse adds a ban on farming just before and just after שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's logic: farming in the seventh year itself is already forbidden by another פסוק. So this פסוק must be teaching something new. The new point is that the ban reaches into year six (plowing for שביעית) and year eight (harvesting שביעית crops), which is exactly adding ordinary time onto holy time.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא is not talking about plowing and harvesting inside the seventh year. That is already forbidden. He is talking about the edges: year six and year eight.

phrases.english: As it was taught: "In plowing and in harvest you shall rest,"
Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר חָרִישׁ וְקָצִיר שֶׁל שְׁבִיעִית,
phrases.english: it is not necessary to state plowing and harvesting of the seventh year,
for it has already been said:
"Your field you shall not sow, etc."
Rather, plowing of the year before the seventh year
that goes into the seventh year,
phrases.notes: Plowing in year six that benefits the seventh year's crops.

phrases.english: and harvesting of the seventh year('s crops)
that goes out into the year after the seventh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא learns from 'בחריש ובקציר תשבות' that the ban on farming reaches into the year before and the year after שביעית, which is תוספת.
steps.raayaObject: The principle of מוסיפין מחול על קודש
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: רבי עקיבא on 'בחריש ובקציר תשבות'

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: only optional harvesting is banned, so the עומר harvest is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל reads the same verse differently. Plowing is always optional, so only optional harvesting is banned. Harvesting the עומר is a מצוה and is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: Just as plowing is optional, so too the harvesting that is forbidden is optional harvesting. This leaves out the harvesting of the עומר, which is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the ברייתא, רבי ישמעאל gives a different reading of 'בחריש ובקציר תשבות'. He uses it to permit harvesting the עומר, not to teach about adding time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל compares harvesting to plowing, since the פסוק puts them side by side. Plowing is never a מצוה, so the harvesting that is forbidden must also be the kind that is not a מצוה. The harvest of the עומר is a מצוה, so it is allowed, even on שבת according to this reading. The result: רבי ישמעאל does not use this verse as a source for תוספת, so a new question is coming about where he learns it.

keyTerms.meaning: Harvesting the barley for the עומר offering on 16 ניסן

steps.whatToRemember: The same פסוק, 'בחריש ובקציר תשבות', gets two readings. רבי עקיבא learns תוספת from it. רבי ישמעאל learns that the עומר harvest is permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי ישמעאל is not saying harvesting is generally allowed. He is only excluding harvesting that is a מצוה, like the עומר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
just as plowing is optional —
so too the harvesting (forbidden) is optional,
excluding the harvesting of the omer, which is a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: מָה חָרִישׁ רְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing reading of the same verse, inside the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only optional harvesting is forbidden under this verse. Harvesting the עומר, a מצוה, is allowed.

steps.title: Where does רבי ישמעאל learn the rule of adding time?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי ישמעאל uses 'בחריש ובקציר' for the עומר, the גמרא asks where he learns מוסיפין מחול על קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל: where does he learn that we add ordinary time onto holy time?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about רבי ישמעאל. He used the verse for something else, so where does he get the rule of adding extra time?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the rule of adding time comes from 'בחריש ובקציר תשבות'. רבי ישמעאל used that verse to teach about the עומר, so it is no longer available to him for this rule. The גמרא assumes he still agrees with the rule and asks for his source.

keyTerms.meaning: We add ordinary (weekday) time onto holy time, starting early and ending late
From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael —

phrases.aramaic: מוֹסִיפִין מֵחוֹל עַל קֹדֶשׁ מְנָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: the rule that we add from the ordinary onto the holy — from where does he derive it?
phrases.notes: He used 'בחריש ובקציר' for the עומר, so he needs a different source.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל מוֹסִיפִין מֵחוֹל עַל קֹדֶשׁ מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from Step 4. Since רבי ישמעאל used the verse for the עומר, he needs another source for the rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source רבי ישמעאל uses for מוסיפין מחול על קודש

steps.title: Fasting begins while it is still day on the ninth
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'ועניתם את נפשותיכם בתשעה... בערב' to mean we start the יום הכפורים fast before nightfall. This proves we add time at the beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from a ברייתא. The verse says 'And you shall afflict yourselves on the ninth.' Could it mean the whole ninth day? So the verse says 'in the evening.' If it says 'in the evening,' could it mean only once it gets dark? So the verse says 'on the ninth.' How do we fit both together? One starts fasting while it is still daytime on the ninth. This teaches that we add from the ordinary onto the holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא about יום הכפורים. The verse mentions both 'the ninth' and 'evening,' so we must start fasting late on the ninth, before dark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בתשעה' by itself would mean fasting all of the ninth. 'בערב' by itself would mean starting only at nightfall, when the tenth begins. Combining the two words gives the answer: start in the last part of the ninth, while it is still day. That early start is the added time.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the verse says (to teach otherwise)
How so? How do we fit both together?

steps.confusionAlert: 'בתשעה' does NOT mean we fast on the ninth day. יום הכפורים is on the tenth. The word 'ninth' only tells us to begin at the very end of the ninth, before nightfall.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for תוספת יום הכפורים: we stop eating before sunset on ערב יום כפור.

phrases.english: He derives it from what was taught in a ברייתא:
"And you shall afflict your souls on the ninth" (ויקרא 23:32).
One might think: the whole day of the ninth?
Therefore the verse says: "in the evening."
If "in the evening," one might think: only from when it gets dark?
Therefore the verse says: "on the ninth."
How so?
One begins fasting while it is still day —
this teaches that we add from the ordinary onto the holy.
phrases.notes: This is the added time at the start of יום הכפורים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 5 by giving רבי ישמעאל's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי ישמעאל learns תוספת from 'ועניתם את נפשותיכם בתשעה... בערב': fasting starts while it is still day on the ninth.

steps.title: Adding time at the end of the day too
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. 'מערב עד ערב' teaches that we also add time when יום הכפורים goes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I only know about its beginning. How do I know we add time at its end? The verse says: 'From evening to evening.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. It now asks about the end of יום הכפורים and finds a source for adding time there as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part only proved early entry. 'מערב עד ערב' links the end of the day to the beginning. Just as we start before evening, we finish after evening.

keyTerms.meaning: Entry; the beginning of the holy day
Exit; the end of the holy day

phrases.english: I only know this at its entry;
at its exit — from where do we know?
The verse says: "From evening to evening."
phrases.notes: The ending is treated like the beginning, so time is added at the end too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בִּכְנִיסָתוֹ בִּיצִיאָתוֹ מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the same ברייתא from the start of the day to its end.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'מערב עד ערב' teaches adding time at the end of יום הכפורים.

steps.title: The rule applies to שבת and יום טוב as well
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא extends the rule. 'תשבתו' brings in שבת, and 'שבתכם' brings in ימים טובים. The general rule: wherever there is rest, we add time.
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I only know about יום הכפורים. How do I know it applies to שבתות? The verse says 'you shall rest.' How do I know it applies to ימים טובים? The verse says 'your rest day.' How so? Every holy day that has a rest obligation, we add from the ordinary onto the holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא widens the rule beyond יום הכפורים, first to שבת and then to ימים טובים. It ends with one general principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each extra word in the יום הכפורים verse is read as including another kind of holy day. 'תשבתו' (rest) includes שבת. 'שבתכם' (your rest) includes ימים טובים. The ברייתא then sums up: any day defined by שבות gets added time at both ends.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall rest; read here as including שבת
Your rest day; read here as including ימים טובים

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי ישמעאל, the source for adding time is the יום הכפורים verse. It covers the start and the end, and it applies to יום הכפורים, שבת, and ימים טובים. Wherever there is שבות, we add time.
steps.confusionAlert: Both 'תשבתו' and 'שבתכם' come from the יום הכפורים verse itself. The ברייתא uses these words to include שבת and ימים טובים; it is not quoting a separate שבת verse.

phrases.english: I only know this for Yom Kippur;
Shabbatot — from where?
The verse says: "you shall rest."
Festivals — from where?
The verse says: "your rest day."
How so?
Wherever there is a rest obligation —
we add from the ordinary onto the holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שַׁבָּתוֹת מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא by extending the rule from יום הכפורים to every day of שבות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'תשבתו' includes שבת and 'שבתכם' includes ימים טובים. Wherever there is שבות, time is added.

steps.title: What does רבי עקיבא do with this verse?
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns תוספת from שביעית, so the גמרא asks what he learns from 'ועניתם את נפשותיכם בתשעה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא: what does he do with this verse, 'And you shall afflict your souls on the ninth'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns the question around. רבי עקיבא already has a source for adding time, so what does he use the יום הכפורים verse for?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes no verse is wasted. רבי עקיבא learned תוספת from 'בחריש ובקציר' in Step 3. So 'בתשעה' must teach him something else, and the גמרא asks what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? What does he learn from it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva —
this verse, "And you shall afflict your souls on the ninth" —
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הַאי וְעִנִּיתֶם אֶת נַפְשׁוֹתֵיכֶם בְּתִשְׁעָה מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבי ישמעאל uses the verse for תוספת, the גמרא asks what רבי עקיבא learns from it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי עקיבא learns from 'ועניתם את נפשותיכם בתשעה', since he does not need it for תוספת

steps.title: Eating on the ninth counts like fasting
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא uses the verse for the teaching of חייא בר רב מדפתי. Since we fast on the tenth, not the ninth, the verse means that eating on the ninth is credited as if one fasted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what חייא בר רב מדפתי taught. חייא בר רב מדפתי taught: 'And you shall afflict your souls on the ninth.' Do we fast on the ninth? Don't we fast on the tenth! Rather, it is telling you: whoever eats and drinks on the ninth, the verse considers him…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא uses the verse for a different lesson, taught by חייא בר רב מדפתי. Eating on ערב יום כפור is treated by the verse like part of the fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא points out a puzzle: the fast is on the tenth, yet the verse says 'the ninth.' Instead of reading this as adding time, it reads it as giving credit. Eating on the ninth counts as if one fasted (the sentence finishes on the next amud: as if he fasted the ninth and tenth). So רבי עקיבא is not left with an unused verse.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
The tenth (of תשרי), the actual day of יום הכפורים
The verse counts it for him (as if…)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the מצוה to eat on ערב יום כפור.

phrases.aramaic: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתָנֵי חִיָּיא בַּר רַב מִדִּפְתִּי.
phrases.english: He needs it for what Ḥiyya bar Rav of Difti taught.
As Ḥiyya bar Rav of Difti taught:
"And you shall afflict your souls on the ninth."
Do we fast on the ninth?
But we fast on the tenth!
Rather, it comes to tell you:
whoever eats and drinks on the ninth,
the verse credits him…
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud: 'as if he fasted on the ninth and the tenth.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתָנֵי חִיָּיא בַּר רַב מִדִּפְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9 by giving רבי עקיבא's different use of the verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא uses 'בתשעה' to teach that eating and drinking on the ninth is credited by the verse like fasting.
